# json-to-express v0.2.0-beta.1

First public beta candidate of the declarative JSON API generator.

## Highlights

- Generate Express or **native Fastify** applications without an Express adapter.
- Choose MongoDB/Mongoose or PostgreSQL/Prisma for full API generation.
- Generate CRUD, relations, authentication (JWT, API keys, sessions, local login, OIDC), workflow endpoints, GraphQL, SDK, admin UI, outbox/jobs, caching and observability.
- Generate multipart local/S3 object storage integration, with immutable upload keys, conditional operation checks and concurrent writer/reconciler regression tests ([#39](https://github.com/ehk2509/json-to-express/issues/39), [PR #40](https://github.com/ehk2509/json-to-express/pull/40)).
- Generate reviewed versioned Prisma migration history, checksums, migration CI, repeatable relational fixtures and deterministic factories ([#19](https://github.com/ehk2509/json-to-express/issues/19), [PR #41](https://github.com/ehk2509/json-to-express/pull/41)).
- Preserve manually created code on safe regeneration using manifest ownership and conflict detection.
- Verify the packaged CLI from an npm tarball as part of CI.

## Try it

From this GitHub tag:

```bash
npm install --global github:ehk2509/json-to-express#v0.2.0-beta.1
j2e --help
```

When the npm registry beta is published:

```bash
npm install --global json-to-express@beta
```

## Compatibility and caution

Node.js >=18; CI covers Node 18, 20, 22. This is a prerelease: JSON specifications and generated application APIs may change before 1.0. Production use requires provider capability checks and environment-specific integration tests. See the README for storage writer and migration boundaries.

**Publishing note:** GitHub release distribution is independent of npm registry publication, which requires registry ownership and configured credentials.
